items.title: Joey Morant interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2013
items.q: Jabbo Smith came out of there, Cat Anderson, most of the great trumpet players, you know, have passed through the orphanage in Charleston, South Carolina.

ctx.x: Well Charleston, South Carolina should have been the jazz center of the world. No, they decided to push slavery, cotton and rice. It’s like I said today, I’ll bet you a million dollars you can’t find 20 black musicians who would have brought this subject up today. I don’t care where they graduated from or how good they look or where they’re going. They don’t want to bring it up. They don’t want to offend anybody. That’s not your concern. If I offend you that’s your problem. I’m telling the story. I hope I offend…

spent way too long wading in the water. You know? It comes from the cotton plantation and slavery. Somehow the music culture of Charleston survived. Thank God. Because of Jenkins Orphanage. You heard about that orphanage? Daniel Jenkins Orphanage. Look up and study on Daniel Jenkins Orphanage in Charleston, South Carolina. Jabbo Smith came out of there, Cat Anderson, most of the great trumpet players, you know, have passed through the orphanage in Charleston, South Carolina.
And you’re going back there very soon.
